title: A Qt Quick TextField backed by an <input>
blurb: A Qt Quick app with two kinds of text field that look the same: Qt's own TextField, and a QML component whose text, caret and selection are a real <input>. The page logs what the browser is given for each: keyboard hints, composition events and autofill attributes.
question: Qt for WebAssembly takes all typing through one hidden input element. If a QML text field is a real <input> drawn into Qt's scene instead, what do IME composition and autofill gain, and can the rest of the QML UI still bind to its text?
result: The binding works both ways. Qt's hidden input has an inputmode and no autocomplete or name, and sits at the corner of the window. The real input has both and sits at the field. A scripted composition deleted typed text in Qt's field. Autofill and a real IME on Android are not verified.
